data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'Maurus', meaning 'dark-skinned'. This name was popular among the Romans due to their association with the Moorish peoples. In Christianity, Morris is associated with the monk Saint Maurice and the miraculous event of the 'Moorish Saints' who were martyred in the late 3rd century. The name Morris carries the meaning “Dark-skinned” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Morris usually hope their child will grow to embody dark-skinned and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Morris total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.
data.cultural_impact: The name Morris has roots in ancient Roman culture and has historical associations with the Moorish peoples. The name's Latin origin, Mauricus, translates to 'dark-skinned' and was bestowed upon individuals of North African or Middle Eastern descent. In modern times, the name Morris is no longer limited to those of Moorish descent, but the cultural significance of its history adds an intriguing layer to its usage.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the name Morris is most notably associated with Saint Maurice, a soldier and monk who was born in Egypt around AD 250. He and his fellow soldiers, known as the Theban Legion, converted to Christianity and pledged to defend the Roman Emperor against invaders. When the Emperor issued a command for his soldiers to sacrifice to the Roman gods, Saint Maurice refused, and the soldiers were executed for their faith. Saint Maurice is now revered as a patron saint for soldiers, martyrs, and Switzerland, where his relics are held. As such, the name Morris carries the spiritual significance of faith, courage, and martyrdom in the face of adversity.
